imageContext:
Image alt: A picture of a wooden structure set in the water on the backdrop of a modern city and mountains is shown. The blue sky is also seen in the far back. In the water, three brown sticks stand upright, the middle one taller and supporting a horizontal brown beam and another rounded beam above. The top of the rounded beam is green and decorated with designs. In between the two beams, a dark brown rectangle sits with ornate gold designs within.

English caption: Figure 12.31 The Itsukushima Shrine. Originally built in the twelfth century, the Itsukushima Shrine pictured here is an important Shinto symbol of the indigenous religion of Japan and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The prominence of shrines such as this shows that the religion is still a vibrant aspect of cultural life in Japan today. (credit: “The torii gate at the Itsukushima Shrine in Miyajima” by Balon Greyjoy/Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0)
